dor_checklist_results.item: Verified real file paths from codebase grounding
Concrete integration spec with existing API contracts
Deploy/doc impact assessed — requires billing provider decision first

assumptions_made.assumption: The billing provider integration will use Stripe, based on the stub imports found in apps/api/src/routes/billing.ts.
assumptions_made.rationale: Stripe is the only provider with stub code in the codebase. However, product leadership has not confirmed this choice, and the issue originally mentioned evaluating alternatives.

assumptions_made.assumption: The subscription model in apps/api/src/models/subscription.ts is stable and will not be redesigned as part of this billing provider integration.
assumptions_made.rationale: The model has been stable for 3 months with no open issues. Assuming it is the contract the billing provider layer should conform to, not the other way around.

alternatives_considered.option: Stripe — webhook-based subscription management with Stripe Billing portal
alternatives_considered.analysis: Full-featured, battle-tested, existing stub code in billing.ts. Strong customer portal UX. Higher cost at scale (~0.5% transaction fee). Fastest to implement given existing stubs. Recommended if time-to-market is the priority.

alternatives_considered.option: Paddle — VAT-inclusive pricing, merchant of record
alternatives_considered.analysis: Better for international customers (Paddle handles VAT). No existing integration code. Requires rewriting the billing route and subscription model. Recommended if the product targets EU customers heavily.

alternatives_considered.option: Build in-house — store card tokens via Stripe Elements but manage subscriptions manually
alternatives_considered.analysis: Maximum flexibility but requires building dunning, retry logic, invoicing, and refund flows from scratch. Not recommended — too much scope for V1.

ui_ux_notes: Billing settings page at /settings/billing should display current plan, next billing date, and a upgrade/downgrade CTA. The billing portal (Stripe or Paddle hosted) should open in a new tab or modal to avoid losing the settings page state. Payment failure should trigger an in-app banner on the dashboard, not just an email.
escalation_reason: The billing provider has not been decided by product leadership. Stripe vs Paddle is a product/commercial decision (pricing model, international VAT handling, merchant-of-record preference) that cannot be resolved by codebase analysis alone. The ticket is fully groomed for both paths; a human must choose the provider before implementation can begin.
recommended_next_step: Assign to product leadership to decide billing provider (Stripe vs Paddle). Once decided, update issue with the chosen option and transition to status:ready. All technical groundwork is complete in this issue body.
